title: Trading in Securities Policy
date_approved: 2024 (Rev. 2, approved by the Perseus Board; prepared by General Counsel & Company Secretary, reviewed by Chairman & CEO)

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: As defined in AASB 124, including the directors, the Company Secretary, the chief financial officer, those persons having authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the activities of the Company, and any other person notified by the Board. Bears all of the substantive restrictions: Prohibited Period ban, prior clearance, short-term trading and short selling bans, Board approval for encumbrances and margin loans, the derivatives criteria in section 10.4 and the notification rules.

tiers.name: Applicable Persons
tiers.description: Directors, employees, advisers and consultants of Perseus and its Group Companies. Subject to the insider trading prohibition, any additional restrictions imposed by the Board or executive management, and (if issued securities under a Perseus incentive plan) the section 10.3 hedging ban on unvested or holding-locked remuneration. Not otherwise subject to Prohibited Periods or clearance.

tiers.name: Related Persons
tiers.description: Applicable Persons' spouses, de facto spouses, parents and children, and entities controlled by Applicable Persons. Key Management Personnel's Related Persons are expressly bound by the Prohibited Period ban, the short-term trading and short selling bans and the clearance regime; for other Applicable Persons the policy only encourages counselling of Related Persons.

definitions.hedging_definition: an arrangement (with anyone) if the arrangement would have the effect of limiting the exposure of the relevant Applicable Person to risk relating to an element of that Applicable Person's remuneration that has not vested in that Applicable Person or has vested but remains subject to a holding lock

windows.start_anchor: two weeks before the release of the Company's quarterly report or half or full year financial statements to the ASX
windows.end_anchor: one Trading Day after that release

windows.start_anchor: commencement of any additional period imposed by Perseus's executive management or the Board when deemed necessary, notified in writing or by email
windows.end_anchor: end of the period stated in the notice, or until the restriction is revoked

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board or Perseus's executive management may impose additional restrictions on Dealing by certain Applicable Persons involved in a potential project or transaction; such restrictions are part of the definition of Prohibited Period. They must be notified in writing or by email to affected Applicable Persons and run for the period stated in the notice or until revoked. The policy does not state that they are confidential, although refusal of clearance must be kept confidential.

rules.detail: Derivatives over fully vested Perseus Securities are permitted only if all five criteria are met: the securities are fully vested; the Derivative matures outside any Prohibited Period known at inception; Perseus is not a counterparty; the Derivative is used to protect the value of an asset supporting a loan taken out to fund the exercise price of Perseus options, or to protect the value of the security against tax liabilities; and the transaction complies with all applicable laws. The Dealing also needs section 7 clearance and post-trade notification with evidence that the criteria are satisfied.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel may only enter into transactions involving Derivatives in respect of Securities in Perseus if the following criteria are satisfied: The relevant Securities are fully vested; The Derivative has a maturity date that falls outside any Prohibited Period known at the time of entering into the transaction; Perseus is not a counterparty to the Derivative

rules.detail: The first criterion in section 10.4 is that the relevant Securities are fully vested, so any Derivative over unvested securities is outside the permission; section 10.2 separately applies the section 206J statutory ban on limiting exposure to unvested remuneration.
rules.evidence: The relevant Securities are fully vested

rules.detail: Securities that have vested but remain subject to a holding lock are treated the same as unvested remuneration; a Derivative limiting exposure to them contravenes section 206J of the Corporations Act, which the policy notes is an offence.
rules.evidence: must not enter into an arrangement (with anyone) if the arrangement would have the effect of limiting the exposure of the relevant Key Management Personnel to risk relating to an element of that Key Management Personnel's remuneration that has not vested in that Key Management Personnel or has vested but remains subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: Section 10.4 is confined to Key Management Personnel. For Applicable Persons who are not Key Management Personnel, the policy imposes no derivative criteria, clearance requirement or Prohibited Period restriction over fully vested unlocked securities; only the insider trading prohibition and any ad hoc additional restriction apply.

The section 206J statutory ban is imported for Key Management Personnel and their closely related parties, covering unvested remuneration and remuneration that has vested but remains subject to a holding lock. Contravention is a criminal offence.
rules.evidence: Pursuant to Section 206J of the Corporations Act, Key Management Personnel and their closely related parties (as that term is defined in the Corporations Act) must not enter into an arrangement (with anyone) if the arrangement would have the effect of limiting the exposure of the relevant Key Management Personnel to risk relating to an element of that Key Management Personnel's remuneration that has not vested

rules.detail: The policy extends the 206J-style ban beyond Key Management Personnel to any Applicable Person who has been issued securities under a Perseus incentive plan, such as options or performance rights, covering unvested awards and awards that have vested but remain holding-locked.
rules.evidence: any Applicable Person who has been issued with Securities under a Perseus incentive plan, such as options or performance rights, must not enter into an arrangement (with anyone) if the arrangement would have the effect of limiting the exposure of the relevant Applicable Person to risk relating to an element of that Applicable Person's remuneration that has not vested in that Applicable Person or has vested but remains subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: Hedging of fully vested, unlocked securities is permitted only through the section 10.4 gateway, which restricts the permitted purposes to protecting the value of an asset supporting a loan taken out to fund the exercise price of Perseus options, or protecting the value of the security in respect of tax liabilities. A hedge for general portfolio diversification or liquidity does not qualify.
rules.evidence: The Derivative is used for the purposes of protecting the value of an asset supporting a loan taken out to fund the exercise price of options granted by Perseus or to protect the value of the security in respect of tax liabilities that may become due and payable

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named, but section 10.4 is a closed list: Key Management Personnel may 'only' use Derivatives for the two stated protective purposes. A derivative structure whose object is to raise cash against, or lock in the value of, a shareholding for general purposes fails the purpose criterion and is therefore not permitted.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel may only enter into transactions involving Derivatives in respect of Securities in Perseus if the following criteria are satisfied

rules.detail: Key Management Personnel and their Related Persons are prohibited from short selling Perseus Securities, defined as selling a security the seller does not own by borrowing it. No exemption route is provided for this ban.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel or their Related Persons are prohibited from short selling Perseus's Securities.

rules.detail: Section 5.2 binds only Key Management Personnel and their Related Persons; the policy is silent on short selling by other Applicable Persons.

Securities lending is not named anywhere and is not within the Dealing definition, which covers only applying for, acquiring, disposing of, or agreeing to apply for, acquire or sell securities. It is referred to only descriptively in the definition of short selling.

CFDs are expressly named in the definition of Derivatives, so they are governed by the section 10.4 criteria: fully vested underlying, maturity outside a known Prohibited Period, Perseus not a counterparty, and one of the two permitted protective purposes. A short CFD would also engage the short selling ban.
rules.evidence: Derivatives has the meaning given to that term in section 761D of the Corporations Act and includes, without limitation, options and contracts for difference (CFDs)

rules.detail: Margin loans in respect of Perseus Securities are permitted with prior Board approval, which is also required for any changes to the arrangement. The terms must not require Dealings at a time when the Key Management Personnel is prohibited from Dealing, and the Key Management Personnel must keep the Company Secretary informed of changes relevant to continuous disclosure.
rules.evidence: The Board's approval is required before Perseus's Key Management Personnel grant any encumbrances or enter into margin loans in respect of Perseus's Securities or make changes to any such arrangements.

rules.detail: Granting any encumbrance over Perseus Securities requires prior Board approval, and further Board approval for any change to the arrangement. There is no outright ban and no distinction by vesting state, although securing unvested plan awards is not addressed.
rules.evidence: The Board's approval is required before Perseus's Key Management Personnel grant any encumbrances or enter into margin loans in respect of Perseus's Securities or make changes to any such arrangements.

rules.detail: Section 10.1 applies only to Key Management Personnel; the policy does not address encumbrances granted by other Applicable Persons.

The policy expressly contemplates 'a margin lending or other secured lending arrangement involving Perseus's Securities' and permits it with prior written Board approval. Section 10.4 also expressly contemplates a loan taken out to fund the exercise price of Perseus options with the shares as the supporting asset. The lender's enforcement sale is an excluded Dealing only where prior written Board approval was obtained at entry.
rules.evidence: If Key Management Personnel or a Related Person enter into a margin lending or other secured lending arrangement involving Perseus's Securities, the relevant Key Management Personnel must keep the Company Secretary informed of any change in circumstances that may be relevant to Perseus's continuous disclosure obligations.

rules.detail: Key Management Personnel and their Related Persons are generally prohibited from Short-term Trading, defined as the purchase and sale of the same type of Securities within a three month period. The Board may exempt in exceptional circumstances on application, following the section 8.2 and 8.3 process.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel and their Related Persons are generally prohibited from Short-term Trading. The Board may on application, exempt a Key Management Personnel or their Related Persons from this prohibition in exceptional circumstances

clearance.approver: Company Secretary, with approval by the Managing Director; where the applicant is the Managing Director, by the Chairman; where the applicant is the Chairman, by the Chairman of the Audit and Risk Committee. Board approval instead for encumbrances and margin loans (10.1) and for Prohibited Period exemptions (8.1).
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (confirmation that the Dealing occurred and the price per Security); directors additionally provide Appendix 3X/3Y/3Z information for ASX filing
clearance.post_trade_deadline: Within two Trading Days of the Dealing; directors within three Trading Days of a change to their interest
clearance.evidence: Perseus's Key Management Personnel are required to obtain clearance for all intended Dealings in Perseus's Securities by themselves or, if they are aware, their Related Persons, at least two Trading Days before such intended Dealings. ... Any Dealing pursuant to this section must occur within 5 Trading Days of receipt of the Company Secretary's confirmation.
Obtain prior clearance for any intended transaction involving Perseus's Securities if the person is a member of Perseus's Key Management Personnel

short_term.basis: purchase and sale of the same type of Securities within a three month period
carve_outs: Board exemption on application in exceptional circumstances (sections 8.2 and 8.3 apply)
short_term.evidence: Short-term trading means the purchase and sale of the same type of Securities within a three month period

exceptions.evidence: The Board may, in exceptional circumstances only, give prior written clearance to any member of Perseus's Key Management Personnel or their Related Persons to sell, but not buy, Perseus's Securities during a Prohibited Period. ... Examples of exceptional circumstances include, but are not limited to: Severe Financial Hardship
Court orders requiring the sale of the Securities in question.

exceptions.approver: Board (prior written approval for entry into the arrangement)
exceptions.evidence: The disposing of Securities: ... as a result of a secured lender exercising its rights under a margin lending arrangement where prior written Board approval was received for entry into the arrangement under section 10.1(a) of the Policy
Entering into a transaction where the beneficial interest in Securities of Perseus will not change

exceptions.approver: prior written clearance in accordance with the Policy
exceptions.evidence: Under a non-discretionary trading plan for which prior written clearance has been provided in accordance with procedures set out in this Policy

The issue of Securities in Perseus under: a rights issue; a dividend reinvestment plan; a share purchase plan; or an employee option plan, employee share acquisition scheme, executive share acquisition plan, performance rights plan or similar arrangement

The acceptance of (or undertaking to accept) an offer under a takeover bid, disposing of Securities under a scheme of arrangement or agreeing to cancel options or performance rights over unissued shares in conjunction with a change of control transaction
Exercising an option, exercising a right under an employee incentive scheme or converting a convertible security.
The transfer of Securities to a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the Applicable Person or Related Person is a beneficiary

The investment in, or Dealing in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme investing only in Perseus's Securities) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party

financing.price_trigger_guidance: Key Management Personnel should ensure that the terms of any margin lending arrangements do not require Dealings in Perseus's Securities at a time when they are prohibited from Dealing; no loan to value ratio or price trigger level is specified.
financing_disclosure: Key Management Personnel: on entry into a margin lending or other secured lending arrangement involving Perseus's Securities, must keep the Company Secretary informed of any change in circumstances that may be relevant to Perseus's continuous disclosure obligations; no fixed deadline
Key Management Personnel: Board approval required before granting encumbrances or entering margin loans, and again before any change to such arrangements (inception and variation)

Key Management Personnel: on use of Derivatives, notification to the Company Secretary under section 11 plus evidence that the section 10.4 criteria are satisfied, within two Trading Days of the Dealing
Directors: Appendix 3X/3Y/3Z information to the Company Secretary within three Trading Days of a change to the director's interest in Perseus's Securities, for filing with the ASX

external_documents: Perseus incentive plans (employee option plan, employee share acquisition scheme, executive share acquisition plan, performance rights plan)
Perseus disclosure policy (referred to in the definition of Inside Information)
exemption_authority: The Board may, in exceptional circumstances only, give prior written clearance for Key Management Personnel or their Related Persons to sell (but not buy) during a Prohibited Period, by Board resolution, written resolution or unanimous email consent; it may impose conditions and will not grant clearance if it considers the applicant holds Inside Information. The Board may also exempt from the short-term trading prohibition in exceptional circumstances. Any clearance may be refused at the Company's discretion without reasons and may be withdrawn if new information or a change of circumstances arises.
jurisdiction_overlays: TSX (Perseus is dual listed ASX/TSX; questions on compliance with ASX or TSX Listing Rules are directed to the Company Secretary)
Corporations Act section 206J statutory hedging prohibition, imported directly at section 10.2
Corporations Act section 205G and ASX Listing Rule 3.19A director notifications

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Derivative is used for the purposes of protecting the value of an asset supporting a loan taken out to fund the exercise price of options granted by Perseus or to protect the value of the security in respect of tax liabilities that may become due and payable.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the decisive clause: a funded collar is permitted only where the loan funds the exercise price of Perseus options or the hedge protects against a tax liability, so a collar used to raise general liquidity against a vested holding fails the closed list of permitted purposes.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Derivative has a maturity date that falls outside any Prohibited Period known at the time of entering into the transaction.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar's expiry and any physical settlement date must be scheduled clear of the Closed Periods, which run from two weeks before to one Trading Day after each quarterly report and each half and full year result - roughly four blackouts a year - materially constraining tenor selection.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Perseus is not a counterparty to the Derivative.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A third party bank counterparty is expressly required, which suits the proposed structure.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Board's approval is required before Perseus's Key Management Personnel grant any encumbrances or enter into margin loans in respect of Perseus's Securities or make changes to any such arrangements.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The security over the collared shares needs full Board approval, not merely Company Secretary clearance, and every amendment, roll or top-up of the facility requires the Board to approve again.

bespoke_clauses.topic: forced sale protection conditional on Board approval
bespoke_clauses.clause: The disposing of Securities ... as a result of a secured lender exercising its rights under a margin lending arrangement where prior written Board approval was received for entry into the arrangement under section 10.1(a) of the Policy [is excluded from the operation of this Policy].
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale is carved out of the Policy only if the Board approved the facility in writing at inception, so obtaining and documenting that approval is a condition precedent to any enforceable security.

bespoke_clauses.topic: loan terms must not force prohibited dealing
bespoke_clauses.clause: Key Management Personnel should ensure that the terms of any margin lending arrangements do not require Dealings in Perseus's Securities at a time when Key Management Personnel are prohibited from Dealing in Perseus's Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Margin call and close-out mechanics should be drafted so that the borrower is never obliged to trade during a Closed Period, for example by allowing cash cure, substitution of collateral or lender-side action.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Short-term trading means the purchase and sale of the same type of Securities within a three month period. Key Management Personnel and their Related Persons are generally prohibited from Short-term Trading.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because Securities are defined to include Derivatives and products that limit economic risk, entering and unwinding a collar inside three months could itself be Short-term Trading, so tenor should exceed three months absent a Board exemption.

bespoke_clauses.topic: securities definition sweeps in risk-limiting products
bespoke_clauses.clause: Securities include shares, debentures, renounceable or unrenounceable rights ... Derivatives and other financial products that can be traded on a financial market including financial products issued or created over securities by third parties and products which operate to limit economic risk in securities holdings.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The put and call legs are themselves Securities, so entry into and unwind of each leg is a Dealing requiring two Trading Days' prior clearance and post-trade notification within two Trading Days.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any clearance under this Policy may be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances. In such event the Company Secretary will notify the relevant Key Management Personnel who must withdraw any outstanding order for a Dealing in Perseus Securities promptly.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Clearance is revocable up to execution, so pricing and signing should occur promptly within the five Trading Day window rather than in staged closings.

bespoke_clauses.clause: In addition to the restrictions set out in section 10.2 of this Policy, any Applicable Person who has been issued with Securities under a Perseus incentive plan ... must not enter into an arrangement (with anyone) if the arrangement would have the effect of limiting the exposure ... to risk relating to an element of that Applicable Person's remuneration that has not vested ... or has vested but remains subject to a holding lock.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank must confirm that every share in the collared parcel is both vested and free of any holding lock, and that no incentive plan participant below KMP level is hedging plan securities.

summary: A funded collar at Perseus is possible only in a narrow form. The secured loan leg is workable: section 10.1 permits Key Management Personnel to grant encumbrances and enter margin or other secured lending arrangements over Perseus Securities with prior written Board approval, and section 6.1(b) then excludes a secured lender's enforcement sale from the Policy altogether, provided that Board approval was obtained at entry. The derivative legs are the obstacle: section 10.4 permits Derivatives only where the securities are fully vested and free of any holding lock, Perseus is not a counterparty, the maturity falls outside any known Prohibited Period, and the Derivative is used either to protect the value of an asset supporting a loan taken out to fund the exercise price of Perseus options or to protect against a tax liability. A collar entered to raise general liquidity against a vested holding does not meet that closed list of purposes and is therefore not permitted, while a collar over shares acquired on option exercise, protecting the asset supporting the exercise-price loan or an associated tax liability, fits squarely. Any such trade needs clearance two Trading Days in advance from the Company Secretary with Managing Director approval, must be executed within five Trading Days, must be notified within two Trading Days with evidence that the section 10.4 criteria are met, and should have a tenor beyond three months to avoid the Short-term Trading ban.
